page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2.16xlarge is a storage- and memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a 64-vCPU dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor based on the x86_64 architecture operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The server configuration features 512.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include dedicated graphics acceleration hardware.

A key component of the hardware architecture is its integrated local storage, featuring 15,358 GB of local SSD capacity directly attached to the instance. For external connectivity and distributed communications, the instance provides a baseline network throughput of 10 Gbps. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled with the instance configuration.

From a cost-efficiency and hardware-density perspective, ecs.i2.16xlarge balances massive local storage capacity against a high memory-to-core ratio on dedicated compute cores. Workloads benefit from the co-location of extensive RAM and multi-terabyte local flash storage without needing external network-attached volumes. This architecture fits large-scale transactional and analytical databases, in-memory data grids, distributed NoSQL datastores, Elasticsearch clusters, and high-throughput data processing systems requiring substantial fast local scratch space.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2.16xlarge is a dedicated KVM-based instance designed for storage-intensive and high-memory enterprise environments. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, alongside 512.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. The server includes 15,358 GB of bundled local SSD storage to support operations requiring immediate low-latency disk access without dependence on network-attached storage. Networking capabilities include a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. With no GPUs onboard, the hardware layout maximizes local density across compute, memory, and high-capacity flash disks. It is suited for large relational databases, distributed NoSQL storage, real-time analytics engines, and in-memory caches.
